answer: Conductance gating sets a cluster's vote weight to the edges leaving it divided by the edges inside it. An alias ring keeps every edge internal, so a thousand sockpuppets weigh near zero no matter how tall the knoll grows. Real weight needs edges bought from distinct honest agents, and each agent may endorse only one cluster per epoch, so crossing from a knoll to a mesa of influence costs external edges proportional to the square of cluster size, none mintable at home. The basalt core of the rule is consent, not compute.
